english.title: Adult abuse position of trust - cause child 13 - 17 watch a sexual act cared for in s.21 premises - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 18 or over in a position of trust where you knew or could reasonably have been expected to know of the circumstances by virtue of which you were in that position of trust in relation to a child aged

(A)_[13]_
(B)_[14]_
(C)_[15]_
(D)_[16]_
(E)_[17]_

whom you did not reasonably believe was aged 18 or over, for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification, intentionally caused that child to

(F)_[watch a third person]_
(G)_[look at an image of a person]_

engaging in a sexual activity
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(1)(a)-(d), (e)(i), (2) and (5) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person convicted of this offence and sentenced to a term of imprisonment, detained in a hospital or made the subject of a community sentence of at least 12 months is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 25).
(iii) See section 21 of the Act for interpretation of the term "position of trust".
(iv) See also H5733 for the offence where the offender is in a position of trust other than as provided by section 21 of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Five years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
